claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform/OpenTofu state backend for Pulumi Cloud.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is an environment variable of the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN may be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud; a separate domain is not required.

The state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name should use the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value in place of `tf.pulumi.com`.
